W2 (empirical), after E020. Tip is E017: 6.548 s, 0.7537, only ~0.07 pp above the 0.753 bar.

Measured chain: E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 -0.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E015 CUDA graphs 0.7574/6.58. E016 wd/2 0.7607/6.58. E017 break-free 0.7537/6.548. E018 24/32 only 0.7502/5.99. E019 rerun of the E016 code 0.7541/6.54. E020 -1 epoch 0.7528/5.86.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: about 0.1-0.2 pp and ~5% time per 0.5 epoch. E020 cost only ~0.1 pp per 0.5 epoch (from E016, ~0.08 from the E017 base), cheaper than I assumed. The dial is roughly linear.
2. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s, the cheapest gain.
3. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s.
4. Time tracks pixel count and FLOPs. Resolution cuts cost 0.07-0.09 pp per 1% of time. Epoch cuts cost 0.02-0.04 pp per 1%, so epochs are the cheapest trade.
5. Width 576->512: -4.8% time, -0.25 pp.
6. LS, Muon lr, LR floor and wd are flat within noise. E016's gain was noise (E019 reran it at 0.7541).
7. CUDA graphs and break removal give ~1% each. The run is compute-bound.
8. Noise: a rerun of identical code is bit-identical, but a math-identical edit reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.3-0.4 pp. Time noise is ~0.5%. The tip's true mean is ~0.754.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and E016 (noise). I over-predicted E018 and was too pessimistic on E011 and E020 time. Time cuts from epochs run about 10% per epoch. Lesson: accuracy differences below 0.4 pp are mostly unresolvable, while time effects are predictable.

Unsure: whether the tip's true mean clears 0.75 on 40 seeds (the E020 trim at 0.7528 suggests it may be near the edge), and whether any free accuracy gain exists.

forecasts.reason: Group 2 narrowing saves ~4% of time at a cost of ~0.2 pp, which falls below 0.753 given only ~0.07 pp of margin; the 0.25 pp loss bound is borderline.
wd is flat within noise; E016 was a reshuffle, so a +0.2 pp gain is unlikely and the result is unresolvable.
Group 1 is memory-bound at the highest res, so removing a conv saves ~6-7% time, but depth loss likely costs 0.3 pp.
A 20 px phase over 15% of steps saves ~3.5% time at ~0.2 pp cost; it is milder than E011 but sits near the bar.

cruxes: What is the tip's true 40-seed mean accuracy? If it is ≥0.755, trims such as -0.5 epoch become affordable; if ≈0.752, the tip is already infeasible.
Is there any accuracy-free speed lever left (kernel efficiency, Muon cost, eval/prepare overhead), or is the run purely FLOP-bound?
How large is the reshuffle noise when architecture changes, and does it exceed the real effect of ~0.2 pp?
